closed_findings.closure: New sticky _ObservationClock wraps the entire observe call including source reads, all attempts and aggregate completion; actual samples are returned without substitution. Between-pair/between-attempt and sticky-sample tests cover the closure.
closed_findings.finding: Attempt-local wall-clock traces could miss a rollback between a first failure and retry, accepting recovered observation earlier than the retained failure.

limitations: No independent pytest rerun, database read, HTTP call, candidate observation, production activation, or live source edit was performed for this review.
The completed old-source probe establishes recurring failures, not a demonstrated V2 recovery gain or CPU/lock causality.
Eight seconds bounds ledger scheduling/queries; mandatory source/envelope verification and synchronous platform operations are separately observed, not a universal hard cancellation guarantee.
review_scope: Read-only scheduling, source closure, failure classification, original identity verification and API cache/consumer boundaries.
AST comparison independently confirmed all original observer helpers unchanged except observe_joint_v3, and all API function/class ASTs unchanged.
Full sorted first pass uses 0.25 seconds per pair; at most one 0.5-second retry inside the same original eight-second ledger budget; no retry of unvisited/missing-publication/integrity failures.

SQLite BUSY/LOCKED require valid clocks and numeric primary code, while INTERRUPT and public pair-budget failures also require actual assigned deadline expiry. Unknown or integrity-related SQLite codes remain final failures.
Original first failure and attempt clocks remain explicit after a new read-only transaction succeeds; no failed row or historical forecast is promoted by rereading.
Native targets expire at actual aggregate completion and recovered ledgers without publication do not count as recovered forecasts.
The new report is capped at two MiB, retains current read observations, and uses distinct V2 source/spec/report/API identities. API refresh/cache/expiry behavior remains unchanged.
